mainTopic: Erased and torn שטרות, אביי's invalid backup deed, and rewriting lost documents
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about a creditor whose loan document (שטר) was erased, and the court writes a confirming document (קיום) for him. A ברייתא gives the exact wording of that קיום. It adds that the creditor can collect without more proof only if the judges wrote that they checked the witnesses and found them consistent. The ברייתא also rules that a שטר that is נקרע is invalid, one that is נתקרע is valid, and an erased one is valid if its writing can still be made out. רב יהודה explains that נקרע means a tear made by a בית דין. He and אביי then give two different signs of such a tear. Next comes a story: landowners in פומבדיתא, afraid of land-grabbers, asked אביי for a second deed. He refused at first, citing רב ספרא's rule against two deeds for one field. Then he had an invalid deed written, and he defended this against רב אחא בר מניומי's challenge. Finally, a ברייתא rules that a lost loan document is not rewritten, but a lost sale deed is rewritten without its אחריות guarantee.

steps.title: End of the משנה: naming the witnesses of the erased document
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes the wording of the court's confirming document by listing the names of the original witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: "...and so-and-so and so-and-so were its witnesses."
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of the משנה, which started on the previous page. The court's new document ends by naming the witnesses who signed the original, erased שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is describing a replacement document that a בית דין writes when a creditor's שטר gets erased. Naming the original witnesses shows exactly which document is being replaced. The גמרא will now give the full wording of this document.

keyTerms.meaning: So-and-so; a stand-in for a real name
Its witnesses (the people who signed the original שטר)

phrases.english: and so-and-so and so-and-so were its witnesses."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה that began on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court's replacement document for an erased שטר names the original witnesses.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives the full wording of the confirming document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that spells out what the קיום for an erased שטר should say.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: What is its confirmation document? "We, so-and-so, so-and-so and so-and-so, were sitting as three judges. So-and-so son of so-and-so brought an erased שטר before us, dated such-and-such a day, and so-and-so and so-and-so were its witnesses."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and quotes a ברייתא that gives the exact text the three judges write to confirm an erased שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave the idea, and the ברייתא gives the complete formula. It records who the three judges were, who brought the document, its date, and its witnesses. This lets the new document stand in place of the erased one.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; introduces a ברייתא
Its confirmation; the court's document that backs up the שטר
Sitting as three; a court of three judges
An erased document

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Rabbis taught: What is its confirmation document?
phrases.notes: "Its" means the erased שטר from the משנה.

phrases.english: "We were sitting as three judges,
we, so-and-so, so-and-so and so-and-so,
so-and-so son of so-and-so brought out
an erased document before us,
dated such-and-such a day,
and so-and-so and so-and-so were its witnesses."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the משנה's short description into a full formula using a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קיום records the three judges, the person who brought the document, its date, and its witnesses.

steps.title: Collecting with or without extra proof
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that if the judges wrote that they checked the witnesses, the creditor collects with no more proof; if not, he must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it also says: "We looked into the testimony of the witnesses and found that their testimony matches," he collects and does not need more proof. If not, he needs to bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a condition: the קיום is fully strong only if it says the judges checked the witnesses and found them consistent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply recording that an erased שטר was brought is not enough to collect on it. The judges must write that they actually examined the witnesses and found their testimony matching. Without that line, the creditor has to prove the loan some other way.

keyTerms.meaning: We looked into; we took up the matter
Matching; consistent
He collects the debt
Proof

steps.whatToRemember: A קיום for an erased שטר lets the creditor collect without more proof only if it says the judges examined the witnesses and found their testimony consistent.

phrases.english: And if it is written in it:
"We looked into the testimony of the witnesses,
and their testimony was found to match" –
he collects, and does not need to bring proof.
And if not, he needs to bring proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, adding when the קיום is enough to collect.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a קיום stating that the witnesses were checked and found consistent lets the creditor collect without more proof.

steps.title: Torn and erased documents: which are valid
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that a שטר that is נקרע is invalid, one that is נתקרע is valid, and an erased or smudged one is valid if the writing can still be seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was torn, it is invalid. If it became torn, it is valid. If it was erased or smudged, it is valid if its outline can still be recognized.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on to other kinds of damaged documents and gives three rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two words that look almost the same, נקרע and נתקרע, get opposite rulings, but the ברייתא does not explain the difference. For erased or smudged writing, what matters is whether the letters can still be made out. The גמרא will next ask what the difference between the two kinds of tearing is.

keyTerms.meaning: Was torn
Became torn
Was smudged or blurred
Its outline can be recognized; the writing is still visible
Invalid / valid

steps.confusionAlert: נקרע and נתקרע look almost the same, but they get opposite rulings. Do not mix them up; the next steps explain the difference.

phrases.english: If it was torn – it is invalid,
if it became torn – it is valid.
If it was erased or smudged –
if its outline can be recognized, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same ברייתא, now turning from erased documents with a קיום to torn and smudged documents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נקרע is invalid, נתקרע is valid, and an erased or smudged שטר is valid if its writing is still recognizable.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two kinds of tearing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of case counts as נקרע and what kind counts as נתקרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of 'torn,' and what is the case of 'became torn'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the two similar words in the ברייתא. This sets up רב יהודה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave opposite rulings for two words that sound almost the same. The גמרא wants to know what actually happened to the document in each case. This is a request for a definition, not an attack on the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?

phrases.english: What is the case of 'torn,'
and what is the case of 'became torn'?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי נִקְרַע, הֵיכִי דָּמֵי נִתְקָרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the two terms used in the previous step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What makes a tear 'נקרע' (invalid) and what makes it 'נתקרע' (valid)?

steps.title: רב יהודה: a tear by the court versus any other tear
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that נקרע means a tear made by a בית דין, and נתקרע means a tear not made by a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: 'Torn' means a tear made by the court. 'Became torn' means a tear not made by the court.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question by tying each word to who made the tear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tear made by a בית דין is done on purpose to cancel the document, so the שטר is invalid. Any other tear does not cancel it, so the שטר stays valid. The difference is who made the tear, not how big it is.

keyTerms.meaning: A tear made by the court
An אמורא who gives the definition here

steps.whyThisMatters: Under this definition, a torn שטר is invalid only when a בית דין tore it to cancel it.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said:
'Torn' – a tear made by the court,
phrases.notes: A court tears a שטר on purpose to cancel it, for example after the loan was paid.

phrases.aramaic: נִתְקָרַע – קֶרַע שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁל בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: 'became torn' – a tear not made by the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: נִקְרַע – קֶרַע שֶׁל בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נקרע is a tear made by a בית דין to cancel the document; נתקרע is any tear not made by a בית דין.

steps.title: What does a בית דין tear look like?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we can tell that a tear in a שטר was made by a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does a tear made by a בית דין look like?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה just said that נקרע means a tear made by a בית דין. Now the גמרא asks how we can recognize such a tear when we look at a שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing that a בית דין tear cancels a שטר is not enough. We need a practical sign that tells it apart from an accidental tear, which does not cancel it. This question sets up the two answers that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?
A tear made on purpose by a court to cancel a שטר

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי קֶרַע שֶׁל בֵּית דִּין?
phrases.english: What does a tear of a court look like?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical signs of the category that רב יהודה defined in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The visible signs that show a tear was made by a בית דין.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the tear hits the key parts of the document
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says a בית דין tear goes through the witnesses, the date, and the core details of the שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: it is a tear through the place of the witnesses, the place of the date, and the place of the core details.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers that a בית דין tears the parts of the שטר that make it work: the witnesses' signatures, the date, and the main details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A random tear could land anywhere. A tear through exactly the parts that give the שטר its power shows that someone meant to cancel it. That is the sign of a בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: The spot where the witnesses signed
The date written in the שטר
The core section of a שטר with the specific details

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
The place of the witnesses and the place of the date
and the place of the essential part.
phrases.notes: The "essential part" is the section with the specific details of this deal, like the names and the amount.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A בית דין tear runs through the witnesses, the date, and the תורף.

steps.title: אביי: a tear going both ways
steps.stepSummary: אביי says a בית דין tear runs both lengthwise and widthwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it is a tear lengthwise and widthwise.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different sign: a tear that crosses the שטר in both directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי looks at the shape of the tear, not at where it falls. A tear that crosses itself does not happen by accident. It shows someone tore the שטר on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Lengthwise and widthwise, like a cross

phrases.english: Abaye said: lengthwise and widthwise.
phrases.notes: These words come from weaving, the up-and-down and side-to-side threads. Here they mean a tear shaped like a cross.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 7, alongside רב יהודה's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A בית דין tear is shaped like a cross, going both lengthwise and widthwise.
steps.whatToRemember: Two signs of a בית דין tear: רב יהודה says it goes through the witnesses, the date, and the תורף. אביי says it runs both lengthwise and widthwise.

steps.title: Landowners ask אביי for a second deed
steps.stepSummary: Arabs were taking land in פומבדיתא, so the owners asked אביי to write them a backup deed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some Arabs came to פומבדיתא and were seizing people's land. The owners came to אביי and said: Please look at our deeds and write us another deed for the land. Then if one is taken by force, we will still have one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story. Landowners are afraid of losing their deeds to land-grabbers, so they ask אביי for a second copy. This sets up אביי's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Losing the deed means losing the proof that you own the land. The owners want an extra deed as a backup. The next step asks whether a בית דין may write one.

keyTerms.meaning: Arabs
Take by force, seize
A Jewish city in Babylonia, home of a major yeshiva

phrases.english: There were certain Arabs who came to Pumbedita,
who were seizing people's lands by force.
Their owners came before Abaye,
they said to him: Let the master look at our deeds,

phrases.aramaic: וְלִכְתּוֹב לַן מָר שְׁטָרָא אַחֲרִינָא עֲלֵיהּ,
phrases.english: and let the master write us another deed for it,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי מִיתְּנִיס חַד – נְקִיטִינַן חַד בִּידַן.
phrases.english: so that if one is taken by force, we hold one in our hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about writing deeds. It ends up connecting to the earlier topic of erased documents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Landowners ask אביי to write a duplicate deed to protect against seizure.

steps.title: אביי refuses: no two deeds for one field
steps.stepSummary: אביי says he cannot help, because רב ספרא rules that a בית דין may not write two deeds for one field.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: What can I do for you? רב ספרא said that we do not write two deeds for one field, because the buyer might collect with one and then collect again with the other.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי turns down the request and gives the reason: רב ספרא's rule against writing two deeds for the same field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A deed is not only proof of ownership. It also lets the buyer collect from the seller's other property if the field is taken away. With two deeds, the buyer could use that right twice, so writing a second deed is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not write two documents for the same thing
Collects by taking back land from buyers

phrases.english: He said to them: What can I do for you?
For Rav Safra said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין כּוֹתְבִין שְׁנֵי שְׁטָרוֹת עַל שָׂדֶה אַחַת,
phrases.english: We do not write two deeds for one field,
lest he collect and then collect again.
phrases.notes: If the field is taken from him, he could use one deed to collect his loss, then show the second deed and collect a second time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי answers the request of step 10 with a no, based on רב ספרא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A second deed is not allowed, because it could let the buyer collect twice.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב ספרא's rule that a בית דין never writes two deeds for one field is a basic rule in the laws of documents.

steps.title: אביי has an invalid deed written
steps.stepSummary: When the owners kept pushing, אביי had his scribe write the deed over an erased spot with the witnesses signing on clean paper, which makes it invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: They kept bothering him, so he said to his scribe: Go write it for them, with the text over an erasure and the witnesses on clean paper, because such a deed is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. אביי gives the owners a second deed, but on purpose writes it in a way that makes it invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The text of the deed sits on an erased spot, but the witnesses sign on paper that was never erased. A deed like that is invalid, so the backup could never be used to collect twice. The owners felt they were taken care of, and רב ספרא's rule was kept.

keyTerms.meaning: Bothering, pressuring
An erased spot on the paper
Paper, here meaning paper that was never erased
Invalid

steps.confusionAlert: Step 4 said an erased שטר can be valid. Here the problem is the mismatch: the text is over an erasure, but the witnesses signed on clean paper. That combination makes the deed invalid.

phrases.english: They kept bothering him,
he said to his scribe:
Go write for them
the document itself on an erasure
phrases.notes: The scribe first writes something, erases it, and then writes the deed over that erased spot.

phrases.english: and its witnesses on the paper, for that is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story: אביי keeps רב ספרא's rule by giving a deed that cannot work.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A שטר whose text is on an erasure while its witnesses sign on clean paper is invalid. אביי used this to satisfy the owners without breaking רב ספרא's rule.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי kept רב ספרא's rule against two deeds by having the second deed written so it was invalid: text over an erasure, witnesses on clean paper.

steps.title: רב אחא asks: maybe the erased writing still shows
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר מניומי challenges אביי: a ברייתא says that erased writing that can still be seen is valid, so the deed written over the erasure might really be valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר מניומי said to אביי: But maybe the old writing's mark can still be seen. And a ברייתא teaches: if writing was erased or smudged, but its mark can still be seen, it is valid!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר מניומי attacks the trick אביי used in step 12. He argues that the erased spot may not make the deed invalid after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's plan depended on the deed being invalid because it was written over an erasure. רב אחא points out that if the old, erased writing can still be read, the ברייתא counts it as valid writing. Then the old writing together with the witnesses' signatures on the clean paper might form a valid deed, which is exactly the second deed רב ספרא said may not be written.

keyTerms.meaning: Its mark is recognizable; the erased writing can still be seen
Was erased
Was smudged or blurred
And it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a source)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Minyumi said to Abaye:
But perhaps its mark is still recognizable,
phrases.notes: He means the old writing that was erased from the paper before the new deed was written on top.

phrases.english: and it was taught: if it was erased or smudged –
if its mark is recognizable, it is valid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method אביי used in step 12 to make the second deed invalid.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that writing over an erased spot makes the deed invalid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says erased writing that is still visible is valid, so the paper may carry a valid deed, and בית דין would end up writing two valid deeds for one field.

steps.title: אביי answers: the erased writing was only random letters
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the scribe never wrote a real deed and then erased it. He only wrote random letters of the alphabet, so even if they can be seen, they are not a deed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Did I say a proper document? I only meant the letters of the alphabet.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his trick. The erased writing was just meaningless letters, so whether or not it shows makes no difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא about visible erased writing only helps when the erased words were the real text of a document. Here the erased writing was just 'אלף בית', so nothing valid is left on the paper. The new deed is still written over an erasure and stays invalid, so אביי kept רב ספרא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A proper, real document
Letters of the alphabet, random letters with no meaning
Merely, just
Did I say...? (a rhetorical question meaning 'I never said that')

steps.whatToRemember: אביי got the owners a deed that looked useful but was legally invalid, so he did not break רב ספרא's rule against writing two deeds for one field.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ: מִי קָאָמֵינָא שְׁטָרָא מְעַלְּיָא?
phrases.english: He said to him: Did I say a proper document?
I meant merely 'alef beit.'
phrases.notes: He means the scribe first wrote random alphabet letters and erased those, so the visible marks are nothing real.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's challenge from step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the case: the erased writing was never a real document.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אחא thought a real deed was written and erased, so its visible mark could make the paper valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only random letters were erased, so nothing valid remains and the new deed is still invalid.

steps.title: A lost loan document is not rewritten
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that if someone says he lost his שטר חוב, בית דין does not write him a new one, even if the witnesses confirm they wrote and signed the original.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If someone comes and says, 'My loan document was lost,' even if witnesses say, 'We wrote it, signed it, and gave it to him,' we do not write him a new document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא on a related topic: replacing a lost document. It rules that a lost שטר חוב is not replaced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the witnesses' support does not help, because they only know the note once existed. They cannot know whether the loan was later paid, and a new note could then be used to collect it again. The ברייתא will next limit this rule to loan documents.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; introduces a ברייתא
A loan document (promissory note)
We do not write (a new document)
We wrote and we signed

steps.confusionAlert: The witnesses are not lying or doubted. They really did write the note. The problem is that they cannot know what happened to the loan after they gave him the note.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: One who came and said,
'My loan document was lost,'
even though witnesses said,
'We wrote, signed, and gave it to him' –
we do not write the document for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הֲרֵי שֶׁבָּא וְאָמַר אָבַד שְׁטַר חוֹבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story of אביי to a ברייתא on the related question of rewriting a lost document.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית דין does not write a replacement for a lost שטר חוב, even with the witnesses' support.

steps.title: Sale deeds may be rewritten, but without the guarantee
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits its rule to loan documents. A lost sale deed may be rewritten, but the new deed leaves out the guarantee (אחריות) that was in the original.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this rule apply? To loan documents. But for documents of buying and selling, we do write a new one, except for the guarantee that was in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא narrows the rule from step 15. It applies only to loans, while a sale deed can be replaced, but only in part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sale deed mainly proves who owns the field, so rewriting it is allowed. The guarantee clause is different: it lets the buyer collect money from the seller if the field is taken away. Leaving it out stops the buyer from collecting twice with two documents, which fits the rule against two deeds for one claim.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case was this said? (introduces a limit on a rule)
Loan documents
Documents of buying and selling (sale deeds)
The seller's guarantee to pay the buyer back if the field is taken away

steps.whatToRemember: Loan document lost: no replacement. Sale deed lost: replacement written, but without the אחריות guarantee.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how בית דין can split one document into parts, rewriting the safe part (proof of ownership) and holding back the part that could be used to collect twice.

phrases.english: When is this said? For loan documents,
but for documents of buying and selling, we do write,
except for the guarantee that is in it.
phrases.notes: This is the clause saying the seller will pay the buyer back if the field is taken from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of step 15 to loan documents and sets a different rule for sale deeds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lost sale deed may be rewritten, but without the אחריות clause.
